newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican banker plays down fears of leftist win.
newsitem.headline: Mexican banker plays down fears of leftist win.

text.p: Mexico's most senior banker, who caused a storm last month when he warned that a victory by leftists in next Sunday's election would cause economic chaos, on Wednesday sought to play down those fears.

"If the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) wins the elections in Mexico City, it's not going to change the condition of the economy," Antonio del Valle, head of the Mexican Bankers Association, said during a meeting of Mexican finance executives.
He said a change in Mexico's economic programme could upset the country's favourable economic perspectives. But he carefully avoided pointing fingers at any party.
"The only risk would be a return to eras now put behind us, an excess of public spending and government intervention in the means of production and services," he said.

In mid-June, Del Valle warned that the PRD's economic platform would plunge Mexico into worse chaos than its 1994-5 economic crisis, saying the party favoured a default on sovereign debt and would spur capital flight.
He issued the warning with the PRD's Cuauhtemoc Cardenas way ahead in opinion polls to be the first elected mayor of Mexico City.

Cardenas's lead grew even greater afterward, polls showed, and analysts said it actually helped his campaign that he was criticised by a banker in a country where millions have been suffocated by bank debts after the 1995 crisis.
The PRD is only likely to win the Mexico City race, though opinion polls say it may also make decent gains in the lower house of Congress, where the 500 seats are also up for grabs.

The same polls predict the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) could lose its 68-year-old majority in the lower house, which would represent a political shake-up in Mexico unseen for decades.
